correctness.rationale: A direct iff proof of pairwise commutation uses explicit witness to one-way dependency and mutual-dependency blocking; the one-pass formula follows without cascading. The closed-set/no-isolated-vertices correspondence is bidirectional. The exchange necessity forces neighboring true twins and hence cluster components, with sufficiency by direct sum of uniform matroids. Union closure is necessary and sufficient for Boolean submodularity of the failure indicator; two-edge forks obstruct it and matchings satisfy it. The labelled counts follow from graph edge choices, set partitions and partial pairings. The accompanying standalone verifier exhaustively checks small sizes, without replacing infinite proof.

value.rationale: Order independence of designated one-head Horn forward-chaining rules is a natural semantic and algorithmic problem; identifying its exact symmetric-dependency graph form eliminates repeat iteration and makes model-fixed sets explicit. The theorem sharply classifies when the resulting closure has the independently meaningful matroid exchange or Boolean-submodular property and counts both families across every finite size. This is more than a textbook count: it gives a necessary-and-sufficient structural translation for two natural closure semantics.
